sectionBreaks.before:
原书以湿黏土、塑料和铅说明较容易留下塑性形变的材料：在所讨论的状态和加载条件下，弹性形变范围可能较小，不大的负载也可能造成永久形变，因此称为“塑性物体”。
这个称呼不是对所有塑料或铅材的固定分类。
温度、材料组成、加载速度和持续时间改变时，它们的弹性、塑性或随时间变化的响应也会改变。
sectionBreaks.after:
弹性物体与塑性物体的划分具有条件性。
同一种材料在不同应力、温度及加载条件下，可以表现出不同的响应；
钢在较小负载下可以弹性变形，达到相应的屈服条件后则会产生塑性形变。

sectionBreaks.before:
锻造是工业加工过程，不是本课要求自行进行的操作。
原书以把铅冷却到 $-100^\circ C$ 以下为例，说明室温下容易发生塑性形变的铅，在较低温度下可以表现出更明显的弹性响应。
这个数值保留为原书的说明，不是所有铅材统一的精确转变温度，也不能据此保证低温下任意负载都只产生弹性形变。
sectionBreaks.after:
脆性描述材料在断裂前只能产生很少的塑性形变的行为；
在本节的拉伸示例中，样品的总形变较小就发生断裂。
玻璃制品和瓷器通常表现出明显脆性，即使从不太高的位置落到硬地板上，也可能因冲击而破碎。

sectionBreaks.before:
原书还列出生铁、大理石和琥珀作为脆性材料的例子。
在通常讨论的材料状态和加载条件下，钢、铜、铅往往比上述材料具有更明显的塑性或延性；
不能据此认定它们在所有温度、加工状态和加载条件下都不会发生脆性断裂。
sectionBreaks.after:
可以利用拉伸时应力 $\sigma$ 与相对伸长量 $\varepsilon$ 的关系，比较脆性断裂与明显塑性伸长后的断裂。
图89和90分别表示原书的生铁和钢样品；
这里沿用以初始横截面积和初始标距计算的工程应力、工程应变，不把颈缩后的局部真应力混入比较。

coverage.topic: Small-deformation elastic recovery versus permanent plastic deformation, conditioned on material state, stress, damage and observation time; no all-material guarantee.
Steel source epsilon1% sample statement retained; rubber tens-of-percent recovery distinguished from Hookean proportionality and nonlinear elasticity.
Wet clay/plastics/lead examples retained; composition, temperature, loading rate and duration qualify the plastic-material classification.
Conditional elastic/plastic classification and steel pressing application retained, no universal common yield limit.
Cold versus hot forging and source lead below-100C retained as source-context illustration, not arbitrary deformation, a universal exact threshold or a child operation.
Brittleness is little plastic deformation before fracture; glass/porcelain/cast iron/marble/amber and contrasting steel/copper/lead examples retained under appropriate conditions.

All source graph89/90 references, stress/strain tokens, original sample values and units retained in order; initial-area engineering stress and initial-gauge engineering strain, rough graph ticks versus prose endpoint not asserted exact.
Small pre-fracture plastic deformation distinguished from slope; no all-brittle equal steepness or strict zero-plasticity assertion.

sourceRisksForMainSCI.original: Steel $\varepsilon=1\%$; rubber $\varepsilon$ of tens of percent described as satisfying Hooke law.
sourceRisksForMainSCI.disposition: Original math token and numerical wording retained. Modern prose makes the steel statement source/sample-specific and distinguishes rubber recovery from linear Hookean proportionality. No formula change or invented erratum.

sourceRisksForMainSCI.original: Cast-iron fracture0.45% in prose; main-provided graph89 risk context is approximately0.5% at the source axis.
sourceRisksForMainSCI.disposition: Prose0.45% unchanged and explicitly source-attributed. Rough graph tick location is not claimed to be an exact matching measurement. No source-pixel rereview, numerical replacement, calibration or figure approval.

sourceRisksForMainSCI.original: Steel at0.1%: $2\times10^7$ N/m2; n50 source steel modulus: $2\times10^{11}$ N/m2.
sourceRisksForMainSCI.issue: Prospective cross-source SCI question: the n52 stress/strain pair implies a secant slope one tenth of the n50 source steel Young modulus if the same linear-elastic material is assumed. The source does not establish identical specimens; this author has not confirmed a printing error.
sourceRisksForMainSCI.disposition: All original numbers/formulas unchanged as source sample values; main may independently assess material/graph consistency. No invented erratum or unsupported replacement.

sourceRisksForMainSCI.original: Steel epsilon1% Hookean example and epsilon0.45% elastic, approximately15% fracture example.
sourceRisksForMainSCI.disposition: Both examples and all quantities preserved as distinct source-context sample statements; not assembled into a universal steel elastic limit.

nativeAuthorCheck.scope: One native author check for this card: normalize_lesson_layout; native adjacent prose_flow anchors; all source-bound validate_text signatures; source/errata binding; math parsing. A native pass is not SCI approval.

figuresStatus: All original figure/caption placeholders and figure/exercise templates unchanged. No source-pixel review, figure context/spec/render work.
limits: Author-only normalized prose freeze. No repeated adapt-prepare, SCI self-approval, source edit/rereview, figure review/finalize, promotion, app/shared-tool/dependency/charter/DB/git/network/browser/other-chat action. Unapproved source mathematical risks are reported, never silently corrected.
